concepts.title: Drainage Basin
concepts.definition: The entire land region that contributes surface runoff to a particular stream network and its main channel.
concepts.key_idea: The total area served by a single river system.
question_patterns: What is meant by a drainage basin?
Define the term drainage basin in geography.
Explain the concept of a river basin.
Which area is referred to as a drainage basin?
Describe the region drained by a single river system.

solution_steps.explain: Locate the primary channel that collects water from various directions.
Follow all smaller streams that feed into the main river.
The outer limit where water starts flowing into this specific system is the basin boundary.

concepts.title: Water Divide
concepts.definition: An elevated landform like a mountain range or upland that separates two neighboring drainage systems.
concepts.key_idea: A physical barrier directing water flow into different basins.
question_patterns: What is a water divide?
Give an example of a water divide in India.
How does an upland separate two drainage basins?
Explain the function of a water divide with a diagram.
Identify the elevated area between the Indus and Ganga systems.

solution_steps.explain: Find the mountain or high ground between two river systems.
Water on one side flows to Stream A, while water on the other side flows to Stream B.

concepts.title: Indus Water Treaty Calculation
concepts.definition: A 1960 agreement specifying that India is entitled to utilize exactly twenty percent of the total water volume from the Indus river system.
concepts.key_idea: Legal limitation on water usage from the Indus system.
question_patterns: How much water can India use from the Indus system if the total is {total_water}?
Calculate India share of {total_water} units of water under the 1960 treaty.
Find the volume India receives from a total flow of {total_water}.
What is the 20 percent allocation for India from {total_water}?
Determine the irrigation supply for India given a total Indus flow of {total_water}.

solution_steps.explain: The total flow of the Indus system is given as total_water.
India is allowed to use 20/100 of the total volume.

concepts.title: River Slope Gradient
concepts.definition: The ratio of the horizontal distance covered by a river to its vertical drop in elevation.
concepts.key_idea: Measuring how gently a river descends over a plain.
question_patterns: Find the distance covered for every meter of fall if the total distance is {total_dist} and drop is {total_drop}.
Calculate the slope ratio for a river stretching {total_dist} km with a {total_drop} m fall.
How many kilometers does a river flow per meter of vertical drop given {total_dist} and {total_drop}?
Determine the gradient of the plains using {total_dist} and {total_drop}.
What is the rate of fall in meters per kilometer for {total_dist} and {total_drop}?

solution_steps.explain: The stretch of the river plain in kilometers.
The total fall in elevation in meters.

solution_steps.action: Calculate distance per meter of fall
solution_steps.explain: Divide total distance by total drop to find the gradient ratio.

concepts.title: Himalayan River Characteristics
concepts.definition: Rivers originating from the Himalayas that are perennial, fed by both rainfall and melting snow, and characterized by long courses.
concepts.key_idea: Perennial flow and intensive erosional activity.
question_patterns: What are the main features of Himalayan rivers?
Why are Himalayan rivers perennial?
Describe the erosional activity of Himalayan rivers in their upper course.
List the depositional features formed by Himalayan rivers.
How do Himalayan rivers differ from Peninsular rivers?

solution_steps.explain: Verify if the river is fed by glaciers (snowmelt) and rain.
Himalayan rivers typically have very long paths from source to sea.
Look for gorges in upper courses and meanders or ox-bow lakes in plains.

concepts.title: Peninsular River Characteristics
concepts.definition: Rivers of the southern plateau that are mostly seasonal, dependent on rainfall, and have shorter, shallower courses.
concepts.key_idea: Rain-fed seasonal flow with fixed channels.
question_patterns: Why are most Peninsular rivers seasonal?
Compare the courses of Peninsular and Himalayan rivers.
Which Peninsular rivers flow westwards into the Arabian Sea?
Where do most Peninsular rivers originate?
Name the major east-flowing Peninsular rivers.

solution_steps.explain: Check if the flow significantly reduces during the dry season (rain-fed).
Most flow east to the Bay of Bengal; Narmada and Tapi flow west.
East-flowing rivers form deltas; west-flowing rivers form estuaries.

concepts.title: Classification of Lakes
concepts.definition: Inland water bodies categorized by their origin, such as glacial, tectonic, riverine (ox-bow), or human-made (reservoirs).
concepts.key_idea: Diversity in formation and salinity of standing water bodies.
question_patterns: How are ox-bow lakes formed?
Distinguish between natural and artificial lakes.
What is the origin of the Wular lake?
Give examples of freshwater lakes in the Himalayan region.
Why is the Sambhar lake important?

solution_steps.explain: Determine if it was formed by glaciers, tectonic shifts, or river cut-offs.
Classify as freshwater (like Dal) or saltwater (like Sambhar).

concepts.title: National River Conservation Plan (NRCP)
concepts.definition: A government initiative aimed at reducing river pollution and improving water quality through abatement works.
concepts.key_idea: Systematic cleaning and protection of national water resources.
question_patterns: What is the objective of the NRCP?
When was the Ganga Action Plan initiated?
How does industrialization affect river water quality?
Explain the self-cleansing capacity of a river.
What led to the expansion of the Ganga Action Plan into NRCP?

solution_steps.explain: Note domestic sewage and industrial effluents entering the river.
The plan focuses on pollution abatement to restore water quality.
